questions.question: A test set has 990 normal cases and 10 fraud cases. What accuracy does an always-normal classifier achieve?
questions.explanation: It predicts the 990 normal cases correctly and misses all 10 fraud cases, so accuracy is 990/1000=99%.

questions.question: A fraud detector has TP=8, FP=2, and FN=4. Which statement is correct?
options: Precision is about 0.67 and recall is 0.80
Precision is 0.80 and recall is about 0.67
Both precision and recall are 0.99
Accuracy is enough to determine both values
questions.explanation: Precision=8/(8+2)=0.80; recall=8/(8+4)=0.67. These expose different costs than overall accuracy.

questions.question: What is the random-ranking baseline for AUPRC when only 1% of examples are positive?
options: About 0.50
About 0.99
About 0.01
Exactly 1.00
questions.explanation: The precision of random selections equals the positive prevalence, so the baseline area is roughly 0.01.

questions.question: How does SMOTE create a synthetic minority example?
options: It copies a majority row and changes only its label
It uses every test target to choose the new feature values
It deletes all minority points before fitting
It interpolates between a minority example and one of its minority neighbors
questions.explanation: SMOTE samples along a segment between minority neighbors, adding variation rather than exact duplicate rows. It belongs inside the training part of a pipeline.

questions.question: A fraud model misses too many real fraud cases. Which change can increase recall at the decision stage?
options: Lower the positive-class threshold and then measure the added false positives
Raise the threshold so fewer cases are called fraud
Report accuracy without changing predictions
Tune the threshold on the held-out test labels
questions.explanation: A lower threshold flags more cases, often recovering positives at the cost of additional false alarms. The threshold should be chosen on training/validation data.

questions.question: Why is Matthews Correlation Coefficient useful for a highly imbalanced binary classifier?
options: It ignores true negatives so it is identical to recall
It uses all four confusion-matrix cells and remains informative when class counts differ
It is always equal to accuracy on a 1% positive class
It can be computed without predictions or labels
questions.explanation: MCC summarizes TP, TN, FP, and FN in a correlation-like score, so a majority-class shortcut is less likely to look excellent.
